title: One Jailbreak to Rule Them All: Output Homogeneity Predicts Cross-Model Jailbreak Transfer

original_idea.body:
# One Jailbreak to Rule Them All: Output Homogeneity Predicts Cross-Model Jailbreak Transfer

**Problem:** If cheap black-box output-homogeneity correlates with jailbreak transfer, the homogeneity that drives systemic risk also makes a single attack fleet-wide.

**Direction:** Measure black-box output similarity between model pairs on benign prompts. Measure jailbreak attack-success transfer between the same pairs. Test whether benign similarity predicts transfer AUROC.

**Why it matters:** A transferable jailbreak across homogeneous foundation models is a correlated, fleet-wide security failure; a black-box predictor is valuable to outside auditors.

**Relevant context:** 'Jailbreak Transferability Emerges from Shared Representations' (arXiv 2506.12913); JailbreakRadar.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a black-box homogeneity proxy predicting fleet-wide jailbreak transfer addresses a concrete correlated-security-failure scenario.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Black-box similarity + published jailbreak transfer measurement; accessible to beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: does benign similarity predict jailbreak transfer AUROC, clear hypothesis.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Black-box transfer predictor for outside auditors labs don't prioritize; no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Black-box inference over model pairs, one GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Jailbreak transfer is studied; using cheap black-box homogeneity as a predictor may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Jailbreak transfer is studied; using cheap black-box homogeneity as a predictor may be open.
